final_answer: ice floats on water because of its molecular structure. water molecules (h₂o) form hydrogen bonds with each other. when water freezes, these bonds create a hexagonal crystalline lattice that holds molecules farther apart than in liquid form. this open structure makes ice less dense than liquid water, allowing it to float. most substances become denser when solid, but water’s hydrogen bonding causes this exception.
